`slurmworkflow` separates a workflow's **design** from a particular **run**. The
design is a directory built in R. Each step has a number, a stable name, a
resolved sbatch submission (`step.swf`), and an optional static successor. The
bash-only engine runs this design on the high-performance computing (HPC)
cluster. Runtime messages can change one decision without rewriting the design.

## Create a workflow

```{r create, eval = FALSE}
library(slurmworkflow)

wf <- create_workflow(
  wf_name = "analysis",
  default_sbatch_opts = list(
    partition = "compute",
    account = "my_project",
    `mail-type` = "FAIL",
    `mail-user` = "user@example.edu"
  )
)
```

This creates `workflows/analysis/`, including the executable `swf` command,
`swf.d/workflow.swf`, and `swf.d/sbatch_rules.swf`. A `partition` default is
required. The options `dependency`, `job-name`, `output`, `parsable`, `export`,
and `export-file` are managed by the engine and are refused in user option
lists. The workflow name must match `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$`.

When the defaults contain `mail-user`, the controller jobs also get it, with
`mail-type=FAIL`: a controller that stops the workflow after a failed step
fails itself, and Slurm mails you (see [Failed steps](#failed-steps)).

The `opt.*` entries of `workflow.swf` are **builder defaults**: they are merged
into each step when it is added. Editing them afterwards changes nothing at run
time. Only the `ctrl.opt.*` entries (options of the controller jobs) are read
when the workflow runs.

## Add named steps

The first step runs bash setup commands:

```{r setup-step, eval = FALSE}
wf <- add_workflow_step(
  wf,
  step_tmpl_bash_lines(c(
    "module load R/4.3.0",
    "Rscript -e 'renv::restore()'"
  )),
  sbatch_opts = list(mem = "16G", `cpus-per-task` = 4, time = 120),
  step_name = "setup"
)
```

The next step sources an R script with variables made available by the template:

```{r fit-step, eval = FALSE}
wf <- add_workflow_step(
  wf,
  step_tmpl_do_call_script(
    r_script = "R/fit.R",
    args = list(n_sims = 100, seed = 42),
    setup_lines = "module load R/4.3.0"
  ),
  sbatch_opts = list(`mem-per-cpu` = "4G", time = "04:00:00"),
  step_name = "fit"
)
```

Unlike `step_tmpl_rscript()`, `step_tmpl_do_call_script()` does not embed the
contents of the script. Its path must therefore be valid on the HPC.
`step_tmpl_do_call()` similarly runs a serialized function with `do.call()`.
Functions execute in a clean R session: all required data must be arguments or
be loaded by the function. A function defined in the global environment loses
that environment when serialized; if it uses global objects,
`step_tmpl_do_call()` and `step_tmpl_map()` warn at build time.

### Step names and successors

Steps live under `swf.d/steps/<N>_<name>/`, where `N` runs from one to the number
of steps, without gaps. A name must match `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$`, have at
most 64 characters, and be unique; `step_<N>` is the default. The directory is
the canonical record of the name. Numbers are positions in build order, not
identities: prefer names everywhere. `add_workflow_step()` refuses a workflow
whose step directories are not numbered exactly `1..N` (for example after a
step directory was deleted by hand).

By default, a step is followed by the next one in build order. Use `next_step`
to make a branch or loop explicit:

```{r static-next, eval = FALSE}
wf <- add_workflow_step(
  wf,
  step_tmpl_rscript("R/check.R", setup_lines = "module load R/4.3.0"),
  step_name = "check",
  next_step = "fit" # Static loop until a runtime message overrides it
)

wf <- add_workflow_step(
  wf,
  step_tmpl_bash_lines("Rscript R/report.R"),
  step_name = "report",
  next_step = NA # End the run after this step
)
```

A numeric `next_step` must refer to a step that already exists and is converted
to its name. A character name only has to be valid syntactically, so it may name
a step added later. Both `NA` and `""` explicitly end the workflow; `NULL`
leaves `next` absent and uses build order.

### Failed steps

**A failed step stops the workflow unless `on_failure = "continue"`.** A step
fails when any of its jobs or array tasks exits with a non-zero status, is
killed (time limit, `scancel`), or cannot start. The controller that runs after
it then submits nothing: it records
`event=error reason=step_failed:<N>_<name>` in the run history, `swf status`
prints `Workflow stopped on error: ...`, and the controller job itself fails
(Slurm mails you when `mail-user` is set). Guards such as a `stop()` in an R
step therefore stop the whole run.

For a step whose failures must not stop the run, for example a map where some
tasks may fail, set `on_failure = "continue"`:

```{r on-failure, eval = FALSE}
wf <- add_workflow_step(
  wf,
  step_tmpl_map(fit_one, scenario = 1:100),
  step_name = "fit_all",
  on_failure = "continue"
)
```

The failures are still recorded in the run's `failed/` directory and listed by
`swf status`, and the next step runs. `step.swf` stores `on_failure=continue`;
the default (`stop`) is not written.

## Map over arguments

`step_tmpl_map()` and `step_tmpl_map_script()` create one Slurm array element
per iterator element:

```{r map-step, eval = FALSE}
wf <- add_workflow_step(
  wf,
  step_tmpl_map_script(
    "R/simulate.R",
    scenario = 1:10000,
    MoreArgs = list(n_reps = 32, n_cores = 8),
    max_array_size = 500,
    array_throttle = 100,
    setup_lines = "module load R/4.3.0"
  ),
  sbatch_opts = list(`mem-per-cpu` = "4G", `cpus-per-task` = 8),
  step_name = "simulate"
)
```

All iterators must have the same non-zero length. `MoreArgs` supplies fixed
arguments. The initial `step.swf` records an array from zero to the slice size
minus one and these data entries:

- `data.map.n_items`: the immutable number of items in `map.rds`;
- `data.map.max_array_size`: the finite per-submission limit;
- `data.map.offset`: the number of items handled by earlier slices;
- `data.map.total`: the number of items enabled for this map execution.

Task `SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID` handles the 0-based position
`pos = data.map.offset + SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID`, that is item `pos + 1` of the
iterators. `array_throttle = k` appends `%k` to the array: at most `k` tasks run
at the same time.

When there are more items than `max_array_size`, array task zero writes a
one-shot continuation with `repeat = TRUE`. It advances `data.map.offset` and
preserves the array throttle (`%k`). Consequently, a dynamic next message
written by `FUN` is honoured only after the last slice, not between slices.
Slices of one wave inherit the wave's override: each continuation is built
from the submission of the slice that wrote it.

Before calling `FUN`, every task validates the `data.map.*` entries of its
submission and checks that the array covers exactly the expected slice (task
IDs `0` to `min(max_array_size, total - offset) - 1`). On a mismatch, for
example an `array` override that does not match `data.map.total`, every task
fails with a message giving both sizes, the array, and the submission file.
Use `set_map_size()` rather than overriding `array` directly. Do not set `array`
in the `sbatch_opts` of a map step: the template sets it, and a different value
is an error.

No sbatch `--export` option is used for this bookkeeping. Array tasks read the
exact resolved file identified by `SWF_SUBMISSION`.

## sbatch option resolution

Workflow defaults, options supplied to `add_workflow_step()`, and template
options are merged in that order. For example, setting `mem = "16G"` by default
and `mem-per-cpu = "4G"` on a step removes `mem` from that step. Giving two
members of one exclusive group in the same update is an error.

The result is written to `step.swf` as `opt.<option>=<value>`. The controller
turns each entry into one sbatch argument; values with spaces, quotes, `$`, `*`,
`%`, `#`, or `=` are not shell-expanded or re-split. Values must be single
character strings or numbers: logical values, factors, lists, dates, empty
strings, and duplicate option names are refused with the option's name.

## Start, inspect, and stop a run

Copy the full workflow directory to the cluster. From the project root:

```{bash start, eval = FALSE}
./workflows/analysis/swf start
```

Every `swf start` begins a new run, with a fresh run directory
(`swf.d/run/<run_id>/`) and log directory (`log/<run_id>/`). Starting again at a
later step with `-s` is a new run too, not a resumption. `swf start` first runs
`swf check`, which validates the step layout and every `.swf` file, and refuses
to start a broken workflow.

The working directory at `swf start` is inherited by jobs. Select another
starting step by name or number with `-s`, or set the working directory with
`-d`:

```{bash start-options, eval = FALSE}
./workflows/analysis/swf start -s fit -d ~/projects/my_project
```

The `swf` executable is the only command needed on the HPC:

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `swf start` | Start a run; use `--force` to stop a live run first |
| `swf stop` | Stop the current run and cancel its jobs |
| `swf status` | Show the run, last submission, queue state, messages, and failures |
| `swf log` | Show the controller log |
| `swf log -s <step>` | Show logs for the last submission of a step |
| `swf steps` | List step numbers, names, and static successors |
| `swf runs` | List run identifiers |
| `swf next <step>` | Set a one-shot runtime successor |
| `swf override <step>` | Build a one-shot resolved submission override |
| `swf check` | Validate the workflow files (also run by `swf start`) |

`swf log` additionally accepts `-t` for an array task, `-r` for a run, `-n` for
the tail length, `--path` for paths only, and `-f` to follow output. Use
`swf help` or `swf <command> --help` for complete options.

Run-specific state is under `swf.d/run/<run_id>/`; logs are under
`log/<run_id>/`. A failing job or array task leaves a marker in the run's
`failed/` directory, and the workflow stops after that step unless the step has
`on_failure = "continue"` (see [Failed steps](#failed-steps)).

Job names and log paths are a public, stable format: step jobs are named
`<wf>_<N>_<name>`, controllers `<wf>_ctrl`, and step logs are
`log/<run_id>/<N>_<name>_<job>_<task>.out`.

### The job environment

Jobs are submitted with `--export=NONE`: a step starts from a bare environment,
not from the shell that ran `swf start`. Load modules and set paths in the step
(`setup_lines`). The engine sets `SWF_ROOT`, `SWF_NAME`, `SWF_RUN_ID`,
`SWF_RUN_DIR`, `SWF_LOG_DIR`, `SWF_CMD`, `SWF_CUR`, `SWF_CUR_NAME`, and
`SWF_SUBMISSION`. Keep state that belongs to one run (counters, flags,
intermediate files) in `$SWF_RUN_DIR`: a new run starts with an empty one.

## Dynamic control flow

A payload can change its successor from either bash or R:

```{r dynamic-next, eval = FALSE}
if (!converged) {
  slurmworkflow::change_next_workflow_step("fit")
}
```

The R function calls `swf next`. Supplying `sbatch_opts` also calls
`swf override` for the selected step:

```{r dynamic-next-options, eval = FALSE}
slurmworkflow::change_next_workflow_step(
  "fit",
  sbatch_opts = list(time = "08:00:00", `mem-per-cpu` = "8G")
)
```

Inside an R payload, these helpers expose the current execution context:

```{r context, eval = FALSE}
slurmworkflow::get_current_workflow_step()      # Number
slurmworkflow::get_current_workflow_step_name() # Name
slurmworkflow::get_workflow_submission()        # Named character vector
slurmworkflow::get_workflow_root()              # Absolute workflow root on HPC
```

**DANGEROUS:** `change_next_workflow_step()`/`swf next` can skip work or create
infinite loops. Make termination conditions explicit and test dynamic paths.
Prefer a static `next_step` when the successor is known at build time, and name
the target step: numbers are accepted, but they are positions, so never compute
a target from `get_current_workflow_step()`. The last `next` written before the
controller runs wins (a replacement is logged in the run history). A stopped
run refuses messages.

## One-shot overrides

Use `override_workflow_step()` or `swf override` to modify the next submission
of a target step:

```{r override, eval = FALSE}
slurmworkflow::override_workflow_step(
  "simulate",
  sbatch_opts = list(time = "08:00:00"),
  data = list(map.total = 20),
  unset_opts = "mem-per-cpu"
)
```

**Overrides aggregate**: an override merges with a pending override of the
same step (the last value of each key wins), otherwise with the step's
`step.swf`. It applies to exactly one submission, then the step reverts to its
saved defaults. `reset = TRUE` ignores the pending override instead. `from`
selects a particular resolved submission as the merge base. `skip = TRUE`
bypasses a submission; `repeat_step = TRUE` runs the target again immediately
after it finishes. `on_failure = "continue"` (or `"stop"`) changes what a failure
of that one submission does. Overriding a map step whose pending submission is
a continuation keeps the continuation's slice unless `reset = TRUE`.

**DANGEROUS:** these are deliberately low-level operations. Repetitions
can loop forever and skips can omit necessary computation.

For a map step, `set_map_size()` safely constructs the common size override:

```{r resize, eval = FALSE}
slurmworkflow::set_map_size("simulate", 100)
```

It preserves the array throttle and resets the map offset to zero. `n = 0`
creates a skip override; `n` greater than `data.map.n_items` is rejected because
the serialized payload has no such items.

## Custom step templates

A template receives the instruction path, template variables, the summary being
built, and the current merged options:

```{r custom-template, eval = FALSE}
custom_tmpl <- function(instructions_script, wf_vars, wf_summary,
                        sbatch_opts, ...) {
  writeLines(c("module load R/4.3.0", "Rscript R/custom.R"),
             instructions_script)
  list(
    sbatch_opts = list(time = 60),
    data = list(custom.mode = "full")
  )
}

wf <- add_workflow_step(wf, custom_tmpl, step_name = "custom")
```

Templates may instead return `NULL` or `list()`. Their `data` names are flat and
are prefixed with `data.` in `step.swf`. The `.swf` format is never sourced or
evaluated; it is parsed as data by both engines.

The result is a portable workflow directory whose design can be inspected with
`swf steps`, loaded back into R with `load_workflow()`, and controlled during an
HPC run entirely through `swf`.
